hypothesis: A 64 MiB original-byte prefix read-ahead with per-tensor materialization may reduce full-layer host memory cost while retaining latency benefits. Compare same prefix serial implementation and native baseline.
limits: OS cache and trial order not controlled beyond randomized two rounds.
Known chunked prefill; no algorithmic novelty claim.
Failure reports retained, no automatic retries.
Byte read-ahead is a known technique; MLX work remains on the main thread. One layer of host bytes is additional RAM, not counted in MLX allocations.
Only a 64 MiB next-layer byte prefix is retained; current tensor reconstruction and MLX tensors are separate allocations. No total-RAM cap claim.
study_kind: Exploratory single-workload transport overlap study, prospectively frozen; no novelty claim.
resource_policy: Use GPU for dense original computations and up to 8 CPU hashing workers, 2048 MiB active MLX check. Existing pressure guards retained. GPU utilization not measured.
